escenas.texto: Thirty videos. Over one hundred and forty-four million views. And one creator with barely thirty-four thousand subscribers who is about to make the giants of Oceania look small. This is Top 10 Social Media, the Oceania edition. Three countdowns tonight: the most viewed, the most commented and the most liked videos of the week. Every number is real, and the name at the top of the podium stays hidden until its moment. Ready? Let's go.

First, the rules, quick and clear. Only videos posted in the last seven days that trended in Oceania. One video per creator on each list. Music and news have their own space. And every number comes straight from the official YouTube API, measured at this week's cut-off. No guesses. Just data.

Countdown number one: the ten most viewed videos. Opening the list at number ten, from Australia, Ken, with a video titled simply “what”. Over seven hundred and forty-nine thousand views, and over one thousand three hundred comments. One word in the title, and the audience showed up anyway.

Number nine takes us to New Zealand. Dolan Darkest, with “How Are These People Real”. Over eight hundred and twenty-four thousand views, and here's the wild part: it was posted on the twenty-fifth of October, the newest upload in this entire top ten.

At number eight, back to Australia. Stimpee, with “The New DayZ Badlands DLC is Brutal”. Over eight hundred and forty-seven thousand views and over twenty-one thousand likes, for a video that runs seventeen minutes. Survival gaming, Aussie style.

Number seven is a marathon. DarkViperAU, from Australia, with “PS3 GTA 5 Was NOT What I Expected - Part 1”. Sixty-three minutes long, and still over nine hundred and ninety-eight thousand views. Just shy of a million, for a video longer than an hour.

Number six, from New Zealand, Viva La Dirt League, with “Ridiculous skill trees in PoE2”. Over one point two million views, and over two thousand nine hundred comments. Remember that comment count, because this channel is not done with us tonight.

At number five, a heavyweight. EYstreem, from Australia, a channel with thirteen point nine million subscribers, with “I Survived 100 Days as VERITY in Minecraft”. A twenty-eight minute challenge, and over one point two million views. The biggest channel on this list, and it's only number five. That tells you what's coming.

Number four, from Australia, Phoenix SC, with “Mojang, what in the actual heck? LOL.”. Over one point four million views and over thirty thousand likes. And now, the jump. Because from here, we leave the millions behind and enter a different league.

The podium. Bronze medal goes to BigKCinema, with “Miles just doesn't care about villains anymore”. Over twelve million views, for a Short that lasts just eight seconds. And the channel? About sixteen thousand subscribers. Eight seconds, twelve million views.

Silver medal, from Australia, Melto, with “Every Home Has A Monster Alarm”. Over twelve million views as well, in a forty-nine second Short, from a channel of about one hundred and forty-three thousand subscribers. Silver and bronze, neck and neck. But number one is in another dimension.

Here it is. Number one most viewed in Oceania: Merry Latte, with “Comment STRAW if you NEED this!”. Over thirty-six million views. Thirty-six million, for a fifteen second Short, from a channel with about thirty-four thousand subscribers. That's almost three times silver or bronze. The smallest channel, the biggest number.

Now we change the scoreboard. Views tell you who watched. Comments tell you who couldn't stay quiet. Countdown number two: the ten most commented. At number ten, from Australia, Bub Games, with “trolling serious military roleplayers in gta...”. Over one thousand two hundred comments, posted on the twenty-fifth of October.
Number nine, a familiar name. Ken, from Australia, with “what”. Over one thousand three hundred comments. One word in the title, a whole conversation underneath.
At number eight, Slushy Noobz, with “We weren't ready for this game...”. Over one thousand four hundred comments on a fifty-eight minute video, and over five hundred and thirty-five thousand views.

Number seven, from Australia, TGG, with a video about GTA 6. Over one thousand five hundred comments, and over six hundred and fifty-four thousand views. When GTA is in the title, the comment section fills up.

At number six, from Australia, Skill Up, with a thirty-seven minute video about the end of BioWare and next-gen console prices. Over one thousand eight hundred comments, and over three hundred and seventy-eight thousand views.

Number five is the surprise of this list. Dejahvoe Ivoe, with “Mass Effect: Universe Trailer”. Over two thousand three hundred comments, and over three hundred and eighty-six thousand views, from a channel with under two thousand subscribers. Fewer subscribers than comments.
Number four, back from the views list: Dolan Darkest, from New Zealand, with “How Are These People Real”. Over two thousand four hundred comments.
Bronze medal in comments, from Australia, Phoenix SC, with “Mojang, what in the actual heck? LOL.”. Over two thousand four hundred comments. Top five in views, and now on the podium for conversation.

Silver medal, from New Zealand, Viva La Dirt League, with “Ridiculous skill trees in PoE2”. Over two thousand nine hundred comments. I told you to remember that number. But even this falls short of number one. Not by a little. By almost double.

Number one most commented in Oceania: from Australia, Dantics, with “I Worked With BioWare on the Next Mass Effect”. Over five thousand eight hundred comments. With fewer than four hundred thousand views, that's more than one comment for every seventy views.
And now, the final countdown. The ten most liked videos, the purest vote of approval. At number ten, from Australia, TGG, with its GTA 6 video. Over sixteen thousand likes.
Number nine, from Australia, DarkViperAU, with “PS3 GTA 5 Was NOT What I Expected - Part 1”. Over sixteen thousand likes. Sixty-three minutes, and people still hit the button.
At number eight, from Australia, Dantics, our champion of comments. Over seventeen thousand likes for the BioWare story.
Number seven, from Australia, Stimpee, with “The New DayZ Badlands DLC is Brutal”. Over twenty-one thousand likes.
At number six, from Australia, Ken, with “what”. Over twenty-two thousand likes. Ken has now appeared on all three lists tonight. Consistency, from start to finish.
Number five, from Australia, Phoenix SC, with “Mojang, what in the actual heck? LOL.”. Over thirty thousand likes. Another channel present on all three countdowns.

Number four, from New Zealand, Viva La Dirt League, with “Ridiculous skill trees in PoE2”. Over thirty-seven thousand likes. And now, hold on. Because the next three jump from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands.
Bronze medal in likes. A familiar face from the views podium: BigKCinema, with its eight second Short. Over two hundred and eighteen thousand likes.
Silver medal, from Australia, Melto, with “Every Home Has A Monster Alarm”. Over two hundred and thirty-four thousand likes. So who could possibly be above this?

You already met them tonight. Number one most liked in Oceania: Merry Latte, with “Comment STRAW if you NEED this!”. Over two hundred and fifty-eight thousand likes, on top of over thirty-six million views. A channel of thirty-four thousand subscribers, number one twice in the same week. That's the double crown.

And the world tour isn't over. Next stop: Asia. The link is in the description and in the playlist. Now it's your turn: which video should have made this countdown? Tell us in the comments with the hashtag Top10RS. Links to every original video are in the description: go support the creators. Subscribe and hit the bell. A new Top 10 every Sunday.
